# About this document {.unnumbered}

The NMEA Cloud Framework describes how vessels, their shore-side shadows and shore services share information in real time,
so that everyone on the water has better situational awareness.

It defines a **common semantic model** — what information *means* —
and keeps that meaning consistent wherever the information travels:
over the internet, over AIS, or across on-board NMEA 0183 and NMEA 2000 networks.

## Status

This is a **living framework document**, not a formal standard.
It changes continuously as the working group develops it.
The version published at <https://nmea-cloud.github.io/Framework/> is always the current one.

Dated snapshots (PDF) are published from time to time for anyone who needs a fixed reference.
A snapshot says on every page when it was taken; check the live version before relying on one.

## How this document is organized

Part I — Overview
: Purpose, architecture, the semantic model and the trust model.
  Everything else builds on this part.

Part II — Vocabularies
: The terms the semantic model is filled with, organized in domain modules that can grow independently.

Part III — Bindings
: How information travels over each transport, and how each semantic concept is represented on it.
  Every binding follows the same template.

Part IV — Applications
: Worked applications of the framework: whale sightings (the proof of concept) and vessel data recording.
  Informative only.

## Conventions

### Normative and informative content

Each chapter starts by saying whether it is **normative** (it contains requirements an implementation must meet)
or **informative** (explanation, background and examples).
Examples, notes and diagrams are always informative.

### Requirement keywords

The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document
are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [@rfc2119; @rfc8174] when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

### Requirements

Each requirement has a permanent identifier and is set out like this:

::: {.requirement #ncf-example-001}
**NCF-EXAMPLE-001** · *Draft*\
An example requirement MUST have a permanent identifier.
:::

Identifiers are never renumbered or reused, so they can be cited safely from implementations, tests and other documents.
A requirement that is withdrawn stays in place, marked *Withdrawn*.

### Open questions

Unresolved points are marked like this, and each should have a matching GitHub issue:

::: {.callout-warning title="Open question"}
An example of something the working group has not decided yet.
:::

## Contributing

Anyone can propose a change — a correction, a new section, a new binding — by opening an issue or pull request
on [GitHub](https://github.com/NMEA-Cloud/Framework).
Human and AI contributors work the same way; see `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `AGENTS.md` in the repository.
